**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. ```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '

final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1620 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1620 - **Title**: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1617` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +1214 - **Deletions**: -36 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T23:02:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T01:57:27Z ## PR Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; ## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1620 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1620 - **Title**: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1617` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +1214 - **Deletions**: -36 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T23:02:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T01:57:27Z ## PR Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

_Previous review discussions for PR #1620._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1620 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1620 - **Title**: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1617` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +1214 - **Deletions**: -36 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T23:02:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T01:57:27Z ## PR Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

# pr-1620: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) ## Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; **ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

# pr-1620: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) ## Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1620 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1620 - **Title**: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1617` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +1214 - **Deletions**: -36 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T23:02:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T01:57:27Z ## PR Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1620._

> ℹ️ **4 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1617 lands as designed: the run-idle watchdog window now derives from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence (entry override > registry > global, floored at `runIdleTimeout`), the zero-byte replay is bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`, and the fire/terminal/notice/banner surfaces name the governing window + source. AC1–AC5 are each covered by real integration tests (43 tests in the PR's verification set pass, plus 145 adjacent ladder/steering regression tests); `dart analyze` is clean. No blocking findings.

**Next Steps**:
1. Wire the queue runtime's failover notices into the `state.model` re-sync (or scope the comment to roles chains).
2. Capture `runIdleWindow` once per arm; fix the doc nit; extract the shared terminal prefix.
3. Note (ticket fidelity, documented in-code): total silent patience can reach ~2× `connectTimeoutMs` when budget ≥ window — a deliberate deviation from I2's letter to keep AC1's replay alive; and the zero-byte terminal text changes even with unset config (per AC5 naming), while kill/replay/abort behavior stays byte-for-byte (AC3).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1620 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1620 - **Title**: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1617` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 9 - **Additions**: +1214 - **Deletions**: -36 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T23:02:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T01:57:27Z ## PR Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).

entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

_Previous review discussions for PR #1620._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1620._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1620._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. In practice the threshold only moves when the **host-configured `runIdleTimeout` itself** is below the ceiling (or above it — never, since `min()`).

Worth one doc line so a future reader doesn't expect `stallNoticeThreshold`'s tight-window branch to fire from a tight `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`:

```dart
/// … keeps its 2m ceiling under a wide configured window. (A tighter
/// threshold is only reachable via a host-configured `runIdleTimeout`
/// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

Both branches render the same `Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} (${windowStory.source})` head; only the connect-budget branch appends the extra clause. Extracting the shared head keeps the AC4 wording single-sourced:

```dart
final head = 'Idle window ${formatProviderTimeout(windowStory.window)} '
    '(${windowStory.source})';
final connect = windowStory.connectBudget;
final windowNote = connect != null && connect.$1 < windowStory.window
    ? '$head; the configured connectTimeoutMs '
        '${formatProviderTimeout(connect.$1)} (${connect.$2}) stopped the '
        'replay budget at ${attemptLog.length} attempt(s).'
    : '$head.';
```

Pure duplication cleanup — the produced strings stay byte-identical (the existing AC4/AC5 assertions in `test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart` and `test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart` pin them).

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "mid-run failover re-windows" claim does not hold on the providers-queue lane**

The comment here says a mid-run roles failover "re-windows the watchdog around the model actually being streamed (AC2)". That is true for **roles chains** — `FallbackNotice` → `_onRolesNotice` (approval_commands.dart:439) re-syncs `_agent.state.model`, so the next arm picks up the new entry's window.

It is **not true for the providers-queue lane** (issue #418): `bin/fah_runapp.dart:792` builds `ProviderQueueRuntime.build(...)` **without `onNotice`**, and `agent_cli.dart:742` syncs `state.model` from `queueRuntime.streamFunction.currentModel` exactly once at boot. A mid-run queue failover (sticky-cursor/cooldown move) therefore leaves `_state.model` on the boot-time entry, and this arm-time window keeps the old entry's patience while the new entry streams. It only bites when queue entries carry **differing per-entry `streamIdleTimeoutMs`** (gh-1398 allows exactly that) **and** the stream is fully silent past the wide window — narrow, but it is the watchdog's actual kill interval.

The ladder-side story is unaffected (`_zeroByteWindowStory` reads the per-attempt model), so AC4 budget math stays correct either way.

Suggested fixes (either):
1. Wire the queue runtime's notices into the same `state.model` re-sync `_onRolesNotice` performs, or
2. Scope this comment to roles chains ("a mid-run **roles-chain** failover…") so the documented claim matches the wired behavior.

Note: ticket AC2 as written (entry override wins over global, per entry) **is** satisfied and tested — this is about the extra mid-run-failover claim in the comment.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runIdleWindow` is evaluated twice per arm — and arms run on every agent event**

```dart
final window = runIdleWindow.window;
_armedRunIdleInfo = runIdleWindow;
```

`_armRunWatchdog` is invoked from `_touchRunWatchdog` on **every** `_processEvent` — including per-delta `MessageUpdateEvent`s on a busy stream. Each `runIdleWindow` getter call does `Uri.tryParse(model.baseUrl)` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (registry walk with a per-entry `Uri.tryParse` + sort). Doubling that per event is avoidable:

```dart
final info = runIdleWindow;
_armedRunIdleInfo = info;
_runWatchdogTimer = Timer(info.window, _onRunWatchdogFired);
```

Same result, half the per-event resolution cost. (Absolute cost is small today, but this getter is now on the hottest event path in the agent.)

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc inaccuracy — a tight `streamIdleTimeoutMs` can never pull the notice earlier**

The comment says "a tight window pulls the notice earlier", but the `window` passed here is `_agent.runIdleWindow.window`, which `Agent.runIdleWindow` clamps to `max(runIdleTimeout floor, explicitIdle)` — a tight configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (say 45s) below the 8-minute floor is raised back to the floor, so the notice threshold stays at `steeringStaleAfter`. /// below the ceiling — the derived window is floored at `runIdleTimeout`.)
```

Behavior is fine (earlier-or-equal notice, never later); this is purely about the documented expectation.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate "Idle window …" prefix across the two `windowNote` branches**

# pr-1620: gh-1617 [GOAL] Run-idle watchdog obeys providerTimeouts: a configured streamIdleTimeout governs silent-stream patience (llama.cpp warmup survives) ## Description Closes #1617 ### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change (verified identical on the base commit and in this runner's environment): the 8 `test/integration/` headless failures (they spawn the real `fa`, which dials this runner's live `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` provider instead of the scripted stream) and a native heap-corruption abort at test-process shutdown (`tcache_thread_shutdown`, fires with this change's tests excluded).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```
